offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 23rd of 32.
offence.blurb: Threw the ball on a higher share of plays than any other team last season, leaning on Marvin Harrison Jr. and tight end Trey McBride while scoring rarely on the ground. With Kyler Murray now starting in Minnesota, it's Jacoby Brissett's huddle, alongside a running back taken third overall.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 29th of 32.
defence.blurb: Struggles to get to the quarterback, with Josh Sweat the main source of pressure, and turnovers come only occasionally. The secondary is young, built around two corners drafted last year in Will Johnson and Denzel Burke.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 30th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chad Ryland was among the most accurate kickers in the league on field goals; Devin Duvernay handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 24th of 32.
offence.blurb: Runs more than most teams do, with Bijan Robinson carrying the load and Drake London and Kyle Pitts the main targets. Passing touchdowns were scarce, and Tua Tagovailoa is the quarterback.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 19th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback about as well as anyone in the league and takes the ball away often, with A.J. Terrell Jr. the established name in coverage.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 24th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Veteran Nick Folk kicks, and returns go to Zachariah Branch, a third-round rookie whose whole appeal is what he can do with the ball in space.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 11th of 32.
offence.blurb: Passed less often than any team in the league, and gained more per carry than anyone: Derrick Henry between the tackles, Lamar Jackson taking plenty himself. Centre Tyler Linderbaum has since signed with the Raiders.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 18th of 32.
defence.blurb: Rarely reached the quarterback last season despite Trey Hendrickson and Nnamdi Madubuike up front, with Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 12th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking rests with Tyler Loop, a sixth-round pick still early in his career, who made a high share of his field goals; Rasheen Ali returns kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 4th of 32.
offence.blurb: Josh Allen is a huge part of the running game himself, carrying the ball far more than most quarterbacks, and this group scored more rushing touchdowns than anyone. Joe Brady was promoted from within after Sean McDermott was fired, so expect continuity rather than a rebuild.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 12th of 32.
defence.blurb: Doesn't generate much pressure on the quarterback, and takeaways are infrequent; the strength is at cornerback with Christian Benford and first-round pick Maxwell Hairston.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 8th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Tyler Bass was one of the most reliable field-goal kickers in the league, with running back Ray Davis doubling up on kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 27th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built around first-overall pick Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard in the backfield and rookie top-ten receiver Tetairoa McMillan, with Ikem Ekwonu at tackle. The passing game gained little per throw and the run game rarely reached the end zone.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 15th of 32.
defence.blurb: Run through Derrick Brown inside and Jaycee Horn at cornerback, with Jaelan Phillips, a first-round pick of Miami's, on the edge. They picked off and stripped the ball reasonably often but rarely got to the quarterback.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 22nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Ryan Fitzgerald was among the more accurate kickers on field goals, and rookie fourth-round pick Trevor Etienne handles kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 9th of 32.
offence.blurb: Caleb Williams is a real part of the running game himself, and the ground game averaged nearly five yards a carry. They gave the ball away fewer times than any other team, with young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 23rd of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that takes the ball away more than anyone else in the league, led by cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, but one that seldom gets to the quarterback despite Montez Sweat on the edge.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 18th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Cairo Santos was one of the surer field goal kickers in the league, with Zavion Thomas fielding kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 12th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-heavy attacks in football, well above the league norm: Joe Burrow throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins produced touchdowns in bunches, while the run game with Chase Brown gained little.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 30th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young secondary with Dax Hill and DJ Turner II that forces a fair number of turnovers, but the front, with Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy, rarely brings the quarterback down.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 9th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Anchored by Evan McPherson, who made close to nine in ten field goals, with Charlie Jones returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 31st of 32.
offence.blurb: Gained less per pass than any other offence and struggled to run, and they are now leaning on very young pieces — Quinshon Judkins, tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and first-round rookies KC Concepcion and Spencer Fano.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 14th of 32.
defence.blurb: A front that sacks the quarterback about as often as anyone, though it forces few turnovers — and it now does so without Myles Garrett, traded to the Rams for draft picks, leaving Jared Verse and Alex Wright rushing and Denzel Ward covering.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 10th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Andre Szmyt made close to nine in ten field goals, with Malachi Corley, a third-round pick of the Jets, taking kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 7th of 32.
offence.blurb: A throwing offence built around Dak Prescott finding CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, with plenty of touchdowns through the air; Javonte Williams carries the ground work behind first-round tackle Tyler Guyton.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 32nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that rarely takes the ball away and doesn't get to the quarterback often, leaning on interior linemen Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark plus corner DaRon Bland; veteran rusher Von Miller has just signed on a one-year deal.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 16th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built around Brandon Aubrey, one of the most accurate field-goal kickers in the league, with KaVontae Turpin handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 14th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw more than almost anyone, though the passes travel for less than most, and Bo Nix's own scrambles are a real chunk of the running game alongside J.K. Dobbins.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 3rd of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass-rushing unit above all — nobody sacked the quarterback more, led by Zach Allen and Nik Bonitto with Pat Surtain II covering behind them — but it forces few turnovers.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 14th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Wil Lutz is among the most reliable kickers on field goals, and Marvin Mims Jr. handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 5th of 32.
offence.blurb: An offence that moves the ball well both running and throwing, with Jared Goff spreading it to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta while Jahmyr Gibbs carries it, and it hangs onto the ball.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 22nd of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback often, with Aidan Hutchinson the centrepiece up front and D.J. Reed the senior man in the secondary, but takeaways come at a fairly average rate.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 27th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Bates is a solid field-goal kicker, with Jacob Saylors returning kicks.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 16th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning offences in the league, with Josh Jacobs doing the carrying even though the ground game gains little per attempt; Jordan Love throws for big yards when he does and the ball is rarely given away.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 11th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that doesn't sack the quarterback much or force many turnovers, now fronted by Micah Parsons, a former Dallas first-rounder, with Devonte Wyatt inside and Keisean Nixon at corner.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 23rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Rookie sixth-round kicker Trey Smack handles the field goals and Skyy Moore returns kicks.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 13th of 32.
offence.blurb: An offence built around C.J. Stroud throwing to Nico Collins, with hardly any push on the ground — few rushing touchdowns and one of the lowest gains per carry. Its real trait is care with the ball: almost nobody gave it away less often.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 2nd of 32.
defence.blurb: Built on pressure from Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter with Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter covering behind them, and it takes the ball away about as often as any defence in the league.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 6th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Anchored by Ka'imi Fairbairn, who made better than nine in ten of his field goals, with rookie draft pick Jaylin Noel handling kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 8th of 32.
offence.blurb: Jonathan Taylor is the centrepiece — this offence scored on the ground more than almost anyone — with Daniel Jones throwing to Alec Pierce, Josh Downs and first-round tight end Tyler Warren. It does hand the ball to opponents fairly often.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 21st of 32.
defence.blurb: A front led by first-round pick Laiatu Latu and Arden Key, with Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward at cornerback; the pass rush is nothing special but they collect a decent number of takeaways.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 2nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking is the strength here — Blake Grupe missed barely anything all year — with Anthony Gould returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 6th of 32.
offence.blurb: Trevor Lawrence's own running is a big part of the ground game, and while runs gained little, the offence still got into the end zone often both ways. Brian Thomas Jr. is the main target.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 8th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that lives on turnovers, grabbing the ball back about as often as anyone, but rarely gets to the quarterback despite Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen. Travis Hunter, taken second overall, features here too.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 13th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Cam Little, a sixth-round pick of Jacksonville's, is the constant, with running back Bhayshul Tuten doubling up on kick returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 21st of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-heavy offences in the league, with Patrick Mahomes throwing to Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce, and adding a fair few carries of his own. Neither the run nor the pass produced many big gains.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 6th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that neither sacks quarterbacks nor forces turnovers much, leaning on George Karlaftis and Felix Anudike-Uzomah up front. Trading All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Rams leaves the secondary rebuilt around L'Jarius Sneed and top-six pick Mansoor Delane.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 15th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Harrison Butker, a seventh-round pick of Carolina's, does the kicking and was among the most accurate in the league, with Nikko Remigio returning kicks.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 20th of 32.
offence.blurb: A pass-first group under Jim Harbaugh, throwing more often than all but a handful of teams, with Justin Herbert also running the ball himself a fair amount. Ladd McConkey and first-round rookie back Omarion Hampton are the other pieces; they rarely score on the ground.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 9th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built around veteran edge man Khalil Mack, this group gets to the quarterback often and takes the ball away at a good rate, with young corners Cam Hart and Donte Jackson behind them.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 5th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking is the strength here — Cameron Dicker made a higher share of his field goals than any other kicker — with Derius Davis handling kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 1st of 32.
offence.blurb: Almost exactly league-average in how often it throws, but it does damage when it does: Matthew Stafford threw for more touchdowns than any quarterback, with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams outside and Kyren Williams carrying the run game.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 10th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young pass-rushing front in Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske, now joined by Myles Garrett and cornerback Trent McDuffie, both acquired by trade — the group already got after the quarterback and forced turnovers often.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 28th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: A thin unit outside of place-kicking, where Harrison Mevis has been accurate; Jordan Whittington, a late-round pick of the Rams', handles kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 32nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Klint Kubiak takes over, so last year's pass-heavy split belongs to the old staff; the ground game gained less per carry than anyone's, and the rebuild leans on rookie back Ashton Jeanty, tight end Brock Bowers and new record-paid centre Tyler Linderbaum in front of Kirk Cousins.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 25th of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that seldom takes the ball away and doesn't pressure the quarterback much, fronted by Kwity Paye, with new head coach Klint Kubiak arriving to reshape what the previous staff left.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 25th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Matt Gay handles the kicking and Tre Tucker doubles up as the kick returner, all under new head coach Klint Kubiak.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 25th of 32.
offence.blurb: Leans on the run more than most teams and gets good yardage per carry through De'Von Achane, but gave the ball away about as often as anyone. Jeff Hafley is new and Malik Willis was signed to start after Tua Tagovailoa was released, so much of this is in flux.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 24th of 32.
defence.blurb: A young, edge-rusher-heavy group built around Chop Robinson, with an inexperienced set of cornerbacks, now under new head coach Jeff Hafley.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 4th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Place-kicking has been the reliable part, with Riley Patterson making nearly all his attempts, and Malik Washington doubling as receiver and kick returner.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 26th of 32.
offence.blurb: A unit that leaned on Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison without much reward through the air last year, and one that gave the ball away more than any other team. Kyler Murray has now been named the starter ahead of J.J. McCarthy, so the quarterback picture is freshly settled.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 7th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built around pressure on the quarterback, with 2024 first-round pick Dallas Turner rushing off the edge and Isaiah Rodgers at cornerback, and they collect a fair share of fumbles and interceptions too.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 3rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Rests heavily on kicker Will Reichard, who made a higher share of his field goals than anyone in the league, with Myles Price handling kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 2nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Gains more per pass than any other team, with Drake Maye also carrying the ball often himself — the quarterback is a real part of the running game. A.J. Brown has been traded in from Philadelphia to lead the receivers alongside Hunter Henry.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 4th of 32.
defence.blurb: A coverage-first group led by cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, with Christian Barmore and Milton Williams inside; they rarely sack the quarterback and don't force many turnovers.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 19th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking is in the hands of rookie sixth-rounder Andy Borregales, who converted field goals at one of the better rates in the league, with fellow rookie Kyle Williams returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 28th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws more often than most teams, which suits a group that struggled badly to gain ground on the run. It is being rebuilt around young draft picks — quarterback Tyler Shough, receiver Jordyn Tyson and tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. — with Chris Olave the established target.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 16th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback well, with long-serving first-round pick Cameron Jordan and Chase Young on the edges, and a young cornerback pairing in Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 32nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking duties belong to undrafted Charlie Smyth, with sixth-round pick Barion Brown returning kicks.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 17th of 32.
offence.blurb: Scores on the ground about as often as anyone, helped by quarterback Jaxson Dart running frequently himself alongside rookie back Cam Skattebo, while Malik Nabers is the main target in a passing game that found the end zone rarely.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 26th of 32.
defence.blurb: Rarely takes the ball away, and is built around third overall pick Abdul Carter rushing the passer plus cornerbacks Paulson Adebo and Greg Newsome II.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 11th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Undrafted kicker Ben Sauls made a higher share of his field goals than any other kicker, with cornerback Deonte Banks doubling up on kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 29th of 32.
offence.blurb: A unit that runs better than it throws — decent yards per carry, but very little coming through the air and few passing touchdowns. It runs through Breece Hall and Garrett Wilson, with Geno Smith, the Jets' own second-round pick back in 2013, at quarterback.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 31st of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that rarely gets to the quarterback and almost never takes the ball away — it had the fewest takeaways in the league. Will McDonald IV, a first-round pick of the Jets, is the man they need pressure from.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 1st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built on kicking accuracy — Jason Sanders missed almost nothing all year — with Kene Nwangwu handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 19th of 32.
offence.blurb: Jalen Hurts is a big part of the running game himself, carrying the ball more than a hundred times alongside Saquon Barkley. With A.J. Brown traded to New England, DeVonta Smith becomes the main target in the passing game.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 5th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets a steady stream of sacks and takeaways without leading the league in either, built around Jalen Carter inside and a young cornerback pair of Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 31st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Elliott's field-goal accuracy is one of the better marks in the league; Will Shipley takes the kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 15th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw a little more often than most, yet get modest yardage per pass, with Aaron Rodgers spreading it to DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. and Jaylen Warren carrying the run game.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 17th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pressure-and-takeaway defence: among the league leaders both in sacks and in balls taken away, led up front by veteran Cameron Heyward and Alex Highsmith, with Joey Porter Jr. at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 20th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chris Boswell handles the kicking, with rookie fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 3rd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning teams in the league by play calls, but when Sam Darnold does throw it goes a long way — only one team averaged more per pass, largely through Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 1st of 32.
defence.blurb: Mike Macdonald's defence gets after the quarterback and forces plenty of mistakes, and it is anchored at cornerback by Devon Witherspoon, just handed a four-year, $132m extension, with Terrion Arnold added on a one-year deal.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 17th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jason Myers is among the most accurate kickers in the league, and Rashid Shaheed doubles as the kick returner.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 10th of 32.
offence.blurb: A pass-first group in effect: Brock Purdy threw for touchdowns as often as almost anyone, while the running game gained very little per carry despite Christian McCaffrey. George Kittle and Deebo Samuel are the other pieces it runs through.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 13th of 32.
defence.blurb: A front that almost never gets to the quarterback — no team managed fewer sacks — and takeaways are scarce too. It is being rebuilt around young players like first-round pick Mykel Williams and corners Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 7th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built on kicking accuracy: Eddy Pineiro made a higher share of his field goals than any other kicker, with Isaac Guerendo handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 18th of 32.
offence.blurb: Baker Mayfield is a real part of the run game with his own carries, and the ball tends to go through Bucky Irving on the ground and Chris Godwin and rookie first-rounder Emeka Egbuka outside; yards per carry and per pass are both low.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 20th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that takes the ball away often under Todd Bowles while the sack numbers sit in the middle, with young corners Zyon McCollum and second-round rookie Benjamin Morrison covering.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 21st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chase McLaughlin is dependable on field goals, and Kenny Gainwell handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 30th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw the ball about as often as any team in the league, but get less per pass than nearly everyone. It now runs through top pick Cam Ward, with fellow high draftee Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson catching and Tony Pollard running.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 28th of 32.
defence.blurb: They get to the quarterback at a decent rate through John Franklin-Myers and Jermaine Johnson, but hardly ever take the ball away, with Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott at corner.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 26th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Joey Slye handles the kicking and 2025 draft pick Chimere Dike returns kicks.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 22nd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning attacks in the league, and Jayden Daniels' own carries are a big part of that; they move the ball well on the ground but scored few passing touchdowns, with Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs the main targets.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 27th of 32.
defence.blurb: They generate a fair number of sacks but almost never take the ball away — only one team had fewer takeaways. The back end leans on young draft picks Mike Sainristil and Trey Amos.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 29th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Drew Stevens does the kicking, with Luke McCaffrey, a third-round pick of Washington's, returning kicks.
